table.name: matches
table.purpose: One row per completed singles match on the WTA (women's professional tennis) tour, mostly 2016-2017, recording the tournament (id, name, date, surface, level, draw size, round), the match itself (score, duration, best-of format, match number), and pre-match attributes of both the winner and the loser (player id/name, ranking and ranking points, seed, age, height, hand, country, entry type).

best_of.name: best_of
best_of.description: Maximum number of sets in the match; always 3, i.e. best-of-three format (standard for WTA).

draw_size.name: draw_size
draw_size.description: Number of players in the tournament's main draw (singles draw bracket size), e.g. 128 for Grand Slams, 64 or 32 for smaller events.

loser_age.name: loser_age
loser_age.description: Age of the losing player in years at the time of the match, computed to high precision (fractional years).

loser_entry.name: loser_entry
loser_entry.description: How the losing player entered the draw (e.g. wildcard, qualifier). Empty in all rows here, so the specific code vocabulary is unverified.

loser_hand.name: loser_hand
loser_hand.description: Playing hand of the losing player: R = right-handed, L = left-handed.

loser_ht.name: loser_ht
loser_ht.description: Height of the losing player in centimeters (range 157-185, consistent with female players).

loser_id.name: loser_id
loser_id.description: Identifier of the losing player; references players.player_id (many-to-one).

loser_ioc.name: loser_ioc
loser_ioc.description: Three-letter IOC country code of the losing player's nationality (RUS, CZE, USA, ESP, GER, ...).

loser_name.name: loser_name
loser_name.description: Full name of the losing player (WTA players such as Svetlana Kuznetsova, Angelique Kerber).

loser_rank.name: loser_rank
loser_rank.description: WTA singles ranking of the losing player at the time of the match (1 = world No. 1).

loser_rank_points.name: loser_rank_points
loser_rank_points.description: WTA ranking points of the losing player at the time of the match.

loser_seed.name: loser_seed
loser_seed.description: Tournament seeding of the losing player (1 = top seed); unseeded players presumably null/0 but not observed here.

match_num.name: match_num
match_num.description: Match number within the tournament (sequential identifier of the match in the event's schedule); not unique across tournaments, so not a global primary key.

minutes.name: minutes
minutes.description: Duration of the match in minutes (0-199; the 0 value likely indicates a walkover/retirement or missing data).

round.name: round
round.description: Round of the match within the tournament: F = final, SF = semifinal, QF = quarterfinal, R16/R32/R64 = round of 16/32/64, RR = round robin.

score.name: score
score.description: Match score in sets, winner's games first, e.g. '6-4 6-4'; tiebreak scores in parentheses, e.g. '6-7(4)'.

surface.name: surface
surface.description: Court surface of the tournament: Hard, Clay, or Grass.

tourney_date.name: tourney_date
tourney_date.description: Start date of the tournament encoded as an integer YYYYMMDD (e.g. 20160815 = 2016-08-15).

tourney_id.name: tourney_id
tourney_id.description: Identifier of the tournament, typically year plus a code (e.g. '2016-M024', '2017-M006'); some rows use a longer legacy format ('2013-W-WT-TUR-01A-2013').

tourney_level.name: tourney_level
tourney_level.description: Tournament tier code. Values I, G, P, W: G = Grand Slam, P = Premier, I = International (WTA tiers), W = WTA Finals/year-end championships. Exact mapping is plausible but not confirmed from data alone.

tourney_name.name: tourney_name
tourney_name.description: Name of the tournament (Indian Wells, Us Open, Wimbledon, Singapore, ...).

winner_age.name: winner_age
winner_age.description: Age of the winning player in years at the time of the match, computed to high precision (fractional years).

winner_entry.name: winner_entry
winner_entry.description: How the winning player entered the draw (e.g. wildcard, qualifier). Empty in all rows here, so the specific code vocabulary is unverified.

winner_hand.name: winner_hand
winner_hand.description: Playing hand of the winning player: R = right-handed, L = left-handed.

winner_ht.name: winner_ht
winner_ht.description: Height of the winning player in centimeters (range 159-185).

winner_id.name: winner_id
winner_id.description: Identifier of the winning player; references players.player_id (many-to-one).

winner_ioc.name: winner_ioc
winner_ioc.description: Three-letter IOC country code of the winning player's nationality (USA, RUS, CZE, ROU, GER, ...).

winner_name.name: winner_name
winner_name.description: Full name of the winning player (WTA players such as Angelique Kerber, Simona Halep, Serena Williams).

winner_rank.name: winner_rank
winner_rank.description: WTA singles ranking of the winning player at the time of the match (1 = world No. 1).

winner_rank_points.name: winner_rank_points
winner_rank_points.description: WTA ranking points of the winning player at the time of the match.

winner_seed.name: winner_seed
winner_seed.description: Tournament seeding of the winning player (1 = top seed).

year.name: year
year.description: Year of the tournament (2013, 2016, 2017), matching the year prefix of tourney_date.

table.name: players
table.purpose: Registry of tennis players: one row per player with identity (first/last name), date of birth, nationality code, and playing hand. Each player is identified by player_id, which is referenced by the matches table (winner_id / loser_id) and presumably the rankings table, linking players to their match results and ranking entries. The ID range starting at 200001 and the mix of historical country codes (FRG) and birth dates from 1943 to 1999 suggest a long-running professional/ITF-style tennis dataset covering both male and female players (given names like Anna, Maria, Caroline alongside Andrea).

birth_date.name: birth_date
birth_date.description: Player's date of birth stored as a text string in YYYYMMDD format (e.g. '19970313' = 1997-03-13). Empty string means unknown. The declared UNION type suggests mixed storage; sample rows show it also appears as an integer like 19430430, but the inferred type is text.

country_code.name: country_code
country_code.description: Three-letter country/nationality code of the player, largely IOC-style codes (USA, ITA, ESP, GER, JPN, RUS, BEL, NED). Some values are historical or non-standard codes (FRG = West Germany, ECA = Central African Republic, HAI = Haiti, HON = Honduras), consistent with a tennis federation dataset spanning decades.

first_name.name: first_name
first_name.description: Player's given name(s); may include compound names (e.g. 'Maria Jose', 'Katia Monserrat'). Never null, though empty string may occur.

hand.name: hand
hand.description: Playing hand: 'R' = right-handed, 'L' = left-handed, 'U' = unknown/unspecified, empty string = missing. 'U' dominates (69%), indicating hand is mostly unrecorded.

last_name.name: last_name
last_name.description: Player's surname, which may be compound (e.g. 'Van Renterghem', 'Delgado Valero').

player_id.name: player_id
player_id.description: Unique numeric identifier for the player; primary key of the table. Referenced by matches.winner_id and matches.loser_id, so each row is a player who can appear in match results. IDs range from 200001 to 220672.

table.name: rankings
table.purpose: Historical world rankings snapshots for tennis players: one row per player per ranking release date (weekly, 1987–2017), giving the player's rank position, ranking points, and number of tournaments counted. Joins to players (and matches) via player_id.

player_id.name: player_id
player_id.description: Identifier of the ranked player. Text-typed but numeric-looking codes (e.g. 200009, 211996). Each player appears on many ranking dates (2776 distinct players over 510k rows). No explicit join was detected, but it almost certainly joins to players.player_id (and possibly matches) — the join metadata simply wasn't captured.

ranking.name: ranking
ranking.description: The player's world ranking position on that date; 1 = best. Range 1–1507, consistent with a professional tennis (ATP/WTA-style) ranking list.

ranking_date.name: ranking_date
ranking_date.description: Date of the ranking publication, encoded as an integer YYYYMMDD (e.g. 20160307 = 2016-03-07). Range 19870119–20170911, i.e. weekly ranking releases from 1987 to 2017.

ranking_points.name: ranking_points
ranking_points.description: Number of ranking points the player held on that date (rolling 52-week points total; max 13615 is consistent with ATP-era point values). Low values dominate because most ranked players have few points.

tours.name: tours
tours.description: Count of tournaments whose results count toward the player's ranking points on that date (0–41). In tennis ranking systems only a limited number of best tournaments count, so this is the number of tournaments included in the points calculation. Alternative reading: number of tournaments played in the ranking period; the two readings overlap and the data alone cannot fully separate them.
